Let <MATH_0001> be a topological space. Let <MATH_0002> be
a category with products. A presheaf <MATH_0003> with
values in <MATH_0004> on <MATH_0005> is a <TEXTITOPEN_0001>sheaf<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>
if for every open covering the diagram
<MATH_0006>
is an equalizer diagram in the category <MATH_0007>.

<STRUCT_0001>
Suppose that <MATH_0001> is a category and that
<MATH_0002> is a faithful functor.
A good example to keep in mind is the case where <MATH_0003>
is the category of abelian groups and <MATH_0004> is the forgetful functor.
Consider a presheaf <MATH_0005> with values in <MATH_0006> on <MATH_0007>.
We would like to reformulate the condition above in terms
of the underlying presheaf of sets
(Definition <REF_0001>).
Note that the underlying
presheaf of sets is a sheaf of sets if and only if all the
diagrams
<MATH_0008>
of sets -- after applying the forgetful functor <MATH_0009> -- are
equalizer diagrams! Thus we would like <MATH_0010> to have
products and equalizers and we would like <MATH_0011> to commute with
them. This is equivalent to the condition that <MATH_0012>
has limits and that <MATH_0013> commutes with them, see
Categories, Lemma <REF_0002>.
But this is not yet good enough
(see Example <REF_0003>);
we also need <MATH_0014> to <TEXTITOPEN_0001>reflect isomorphisms<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>.
This property means that given a morphism
<MATH_0015> in <MATH_0016>, then <MATH_0017> is
an isomorphism if (and only if) <MATH_0018> is a bijection.
